en-US.author: doaipm
en-US.description: Free, fast, cross-platform archiver (ZIP/RAR/7z/tar/ISO) with a desktop app, CLI and MCP server.
en-US.longDescription:
Ziplark extracts ZIP, RAR (incl. RAR5 and encrypted), 7z, tar, the compressed-tar
variants (tar.gz/.bz2/.xz/.zst/.lz4), single-stream gz/bz2/xz/zst/lz4, and ISO 9660 /
Joliet disc images. It creates ZIP (AES-256), 7z (AES-256) and tar archives.

One small Rust engine drives three front-ends over the exact same code: a desktop app,
the ziplark command-line tool, and an MCP server so an LLM or agent can list, extract,
test and create archives itself.

Every extraction path is funnelled through a single zip-slip guard, so no entry can
escape the destination directory. Free and open source (MIT), no ads, no telemetry.
en-US.name: Ziplark
en-US.releaseNotes:
The preview, smart-extract, package-format & desktop experience release.
Added
- Read and preview files inside an archive without extracting.
  ziplark_core::read_entry streams a single entry into memory with optional
  offset and max_bytes bounds — including from RAR/RAR5 (via UCM_PROCESSDATA
  during RAR_TEST) and ISO 9660. Exposed across all three interfaces:
  - Desktop app: Double-click any file to open the Quick Preview modal
    (UTF-8 text/code viewer, inline image preview for PNG/JPG/GIF/WebP/SVG/BMP/ICO,
    or hex/ASCII dump for binaries).
  - CLI: ziplark cat <archive> <entry> (alias read) streams to stdout or
    returns structured JSON (--json, --offset, --max-bytes).
  - MCP: ziplark_read is a read-only tool (available even without
    --allow-write) that returns UTF-8 text or hex preview with offset /
    max_bytes paging so LLMs can inspect source files inside archives directly.
- Live search & column sorting in the desktop app. Instant filter bar with
  recursive search across the archive, keyboard shortcut (⌘F / Ctrl+F), and
  clickable column headers to sort by Name, Modified, or Size
  (directories always stay grouped on top).
- Smart extraction (--smart & "Extract Here"). Automatically inspects the
  archive's top-level layout: multi-root archives ("tarbombs") are wrapped into a
  clean <archive-stem>/ subfolder, whereas single-root archives extract
  directly without creating redundant <stem>/<stem>/ nesting, and existing
  files are protected by automatic <stem> (2) disambiguation. Available via
  ziplark extract --smart, ziplark extract-here, MCP ziplark_extract
  ("smart": true), and the new Extract Here button in the desktop app.
- Multi-volume .7z.001, .zip.001 and PKWARE split .z01 + .zip archives.
  Opening any part resolves the full volume set, lists all parts on disk, and
  extracts entries spanning across volumes. Missing .7z.002+ volumes are
  detected upfront from the 7z signature header's expected archive size, and
  PKWARE split .z01 + .zip central directory disk numbers & offsets are
  translated in memory.
- New archive and system package formats (dependency-free pure Rust):
  - Unix ar / static libraries (.ar, .a, .lib) — supports both GNU
    (// string table) and BSD (#1/<len>) extended filenames.
  - Debian packages (.deb, .udeb, .ipk) — transparently traverses the
    outer ar container and both inner data.tar.* and control.tar.*
    (exposed under DEBIAN/) archives (gz, xz, zst, bz2, lz4, or
    uncompressed).
  - CPIO archives (.cpio, .cpio.gz, .cpio.xz, .cpio.zst, .cpio.bz2, .cpio.lz4) —
    supports SVR4 070701 (newc), 070702 (crc) and POSIX 070707 (odc).
  - RPM packages (.rpm, .srpm) — parses the 96-byte Lead, Signature
    Header and Main Header, and decompresses the embedded CPIO payload (gzip,
    xz, zstd, bzip2, lz4).
  - Microsoft Cabinet (.cab) — parses CFHEADER, CFFOLDER, CFFILE and
    CFDATA blocks with Store and MSZIP (Deflate CK + 32 KiB sliding dictionary
    history across blocks in a folder).
  - Application & document containers — .crx (Chrome extensions, skipping
    CRX2/CRX3 headers before the ZIP payload), .jar, .war, .ear, .apk,
    .ipa, .aab, .whl, .egg, .nupkg, .vsix, .xpi, .epub, .docx,
    .xlsx, .pptx, .odt, .ods, .odp, .cbz, .cbr, .cb7, .cbt.
- In-place archive append (ziplark add). Add or update files inside an
  existing .zip (fast raw-stream copy for unchanged entries), .7z, .tar,
  or .tar.<ext> archive via ziplark add <archive> <inputs...>, MCP
  ziplark_add, or the desktop app's Add files… button and drag-and-drop.
- One-click OS Right-Click Context Menu manager in the desktop app. Install,
  inspect, or remove Finder Quick Actions (macOS), Explorer context-menu verbs
  (Windows), and Dolphin/Nautilus scripts (Linux) directly from the GUI header,
  backed by headless extract-here / compress-zip support in the GUI binary
  itself.
- 9-language UI localization. Added Traditional Chinese (zh-TW), Japanese
  (ja), Korean (ko), Spanish (es), French (fr), German (de), and
  Russian (ru) alongside English (en) and Simplified Chinese (zh-CN).
- An MCP Bundle (.mcpb) ships with every release, carrying the server for
  macOS (universal), Windows and Linux in one artifact, and Ziplark is listed in
  the official MCP registry as io.github.zhitongblog/ziplark.
Downloads. ziplark-v0.4.0-<target>.tar.gz / .zip hold the ziplark CLI and the ziplark-mcp server (checksums beside them). Desktop: .msi/.exe for Windows, .deb/.AppImage for Linux. macOS: brew install --cask zhitongblog/tap/ziplark, or the signed & notarized Ziplark-v0.4.0-macos-universal.dmg.
Full changelog: https://github.com/zhitongblog/ziplark/blob/v0.4.0/CHANGELOG.md
